timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: June opened her Las Vegas workshop by throwing a wrench at my feet. "There," she said. "Ceremony complete." I looked down at the wrench. Then at the ribbon stretched across the garage doors. "Nigga, I bought scissors." "You also bought a car and drove it onto a tank.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: We are all disappointed sometimes." Adrian stood beside her wearing a clean shirt that had already lost an argument with engine grease. Behind them, the Last Word rested under bright lights with its hood removed. My magnificent blue car looked like a rich patient being introduced to specialists. Shawna examined the new sign above the doors. MERCURY & ADRIAN.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Below it, in smaller letters: CARS WORTH COMING HOME IN. She took June's hand. "That's good." June looked up at the sign and smiled in a way I had not seen when she first came down the spillway in the desert. Back then the nigga with the palace had been trying to take the ground beneath her feet.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Now she owned the old garage, a Las Vegas branch, and enough equipment to make Adrian occasionally walk into a room and laugh at a lift. "We go back after the wedding," she said. "Open the desert shop properly. Hire the men Zero kept stealing away. Then split our time." "And my car?" I asked.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "Your car learns patience." "Nigga, it didn't come with that feature." "Neither did its owner. I'm expanding both." The staff gathered around us: grown mechanics, apprentices in their twenties, drivers who had watched June bring a car out of war and wanted to learn how she listened to an engine.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: They stared at me with the careful excitement of people trying to look professional around a man whose worst parking choices had become their favorite videos. One mechanic raised a hand. "Captain, can I ask about the armored vehicle?" June closed her eyes.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "Nigga, do not encourage the customer." "Technically," I said, "I used its roof as temporary road surface." The young man nodded like I had handed him a sacred engineering principle. Adrian laughed so hard he had to sit down. We cut the ribbon with the scissors anyway. June let me keep the wrench. I considered that affection.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Across town, Mercedes and Porsche were opening something louder. Their building had once been an expensive restaurant run by a man who confused low lighting with good food. Now its windows shone red and blue. Music came through the doors. A neon sign above the entrance read TWO NAMES YOU REMEMBER.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Inside, women in silk and men in sharp suits moved between a small stage, a bar, and tables set far enough apart for people to tell outrageous stories without borrowing the next table's secrets. The place belonged to Mercedes and Porsche together.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Music nights, private parties, performances, an agency upstairs for the adult entertainers who wanted to choose their own bookings and keep people they trusted nearby. They had made it beautiful. They had also put a framed photograph of me in the men's bathroom. I discovered that before the ribbon ceremony. "Niggas," I called when I came back out. Mercedes smiled.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Porsche tried to look innocent and failed at a professional level. "Why am I above the sinks?" "Inspiration," Porsche said. "For what?" "Standards," Mercedes replied. Shawna went to look. When she returned, she was laughing too hard to speak. "They chose a good photograph," she managed. "Nigga, I look like I'm supervising handwashing." "Public service," Knox said from the bar. Everybody laughed.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: The opening party filled the place by eight. Sex workers I had known from the old Vegas nights came with friends, dates, husbands, girlfriends, and stories that got louder every time somebody bought another bottle. One woman told Mercedes she once charged a millionaire extra because he kept interrupting a perfectly good evening to explain his golf swing.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Another said she had left a man in a hotel lobby after he introduced his watch before introducing himself. "What watch?" Tank asked. Rosa stared at him. "Nigga, that is not the moral of the story." "I was assessing the situation." The woman laughed. "Ugly watch." Tank nodded solemnly.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "Then you made the correct decision." Shawna sat beside me, one hand on my thigh, listening as the women talked. Nobody asked them to become symbols of anything. They were funny, tired, ambitious, vain, generous, occasionally full of shit, and very good at recognizing a man who believed paying for an evening meant buying the whole person standing inside it. Porsche raised a glass.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "To choosing the room." Mercedes lifted hers. "And knowing where the exits are." I raised mine with them. "Niggas, may the money be rude and the company worth it." The table cheered. Sienna played the first set with her sister. Rosa joined for two songs.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Shawna joined for a third, and suddenly the room belonged to the women who had carried music out of the emperor's palace and brought it somewhere the doors opened from the inside. Mercedes stood beside me watching the stage. "You like it?" "Nigga, I love it." Her face softened before she caught herself. "Good.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Because your first table is expensive." "I helped buy the building." "And now you support the business. Growth." I laughed and kissed her cheek. "You got it." At the track the next afternoon, Inez drove Sol de Abril with her father in the passenger seat. Esteban had flown in for the wedding.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Cassius's father, Nero, came too, walking with the measured care of a man who had survived enough captivity to value every unnecessary step he could take outside. The two old racers stood together in the pit lane before the run, inspecting the silver car like it had returned from a war they remembered in different pieces.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: When the engine started, Esteban put a hand against the hood. He did not speak for a long moment. Inez waited. Then he looked at her. "You drive." She smiled. Nigga, the woman could make a whole grandstand nervous without moving. That smile was softer than any victory I had seen her win. They went around the track once slowly. Then she accelerated.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Esteban's laugh came over the open radio. Cassius stood beside me with his arms folded, watching the car disappear into the turn. "You look stupid," I told him. "I am in love." "Nigga, I recognized the condition. I was discussing the face." He laughed without looking away.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "I am going to ask her to build a team with me." "You already racing together." "A real team. Our name on the garage. Our drivers. Our cars. Our choices." "And a ring?" He looked at me. "Eventually." "Nigga, you say eventually like it's a country you'll visit after the weather improves." He rubbed his jaw.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "I don't want to make winning her feel like winning a race." That stopped my joke before it reached my mouth. I looked at the track. At the silver car coming back into view, Inez laughing beside her father. "Then don't ask like a man expecting a trophy," I said.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "Ask like a nigga who wants somebody beside him when the engine's off." Cassius nodded slowly. When Inez brought the car in, he went to her before she had taken off her gloves. I did not hear what he said. I saw her expression change.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Then I saw her put both hands on his face and kiss him in the middle of the pit lane while Esteban climbed out of the passenger seat pretending very hard to admire the tires. Nero stood beside him. "Young people," he said. Esteban nodded. "Terrible at discretion." The two men smiled like niggas who had never once practiced it themselves.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: That evening, Vesper came to the mansion with Magnolia and Bernard. She wore a simple dark dress and carried no folio. For the first time since the desert, she looked like a woman arriving for dinner instead of an argument that might require cavalry. Shawna met her at the door. They embraced.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: I watched from the stairs with the strange pleasure of seeing two women who had every reason to misunderstand each other choose not to make that anybody's entertainment. Vesper gave me a small box. Inside was a silver key. "The Blue House," she said. "Bastien asked me to bring it.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: There will always be a room for you in Midnight City." "Nigga, tell him make it a large room." "He already knows your luggage habits." I smiled. "How is he?" "Arguing with Madame Caron about curtains. Recovering his territory by annoying her into surrender." "Healthy, then." "Very." We sat outside while the garden lights came on. Bernard talked with June about the hotel plans.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Magnolia corrected both of them on the placement of benches. Vesper watched the white horse move beyond the fence. "You could have kept the Last City," she said quietly. "I kept enough." She looked at me. "That answer would once have surprised me." I pointed toward the driveway, where three newly arrived cars waited beneath covers.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "Nigga, don't become sentimental before checking the parking." She laughed. Then she looked toward Shawna, who stood with Rosa by the kitchen doors, arguing lovingly about wedding music. "You know what you want." "Most days." "And on the others?" "She reminds me. Loudly." Vesper smiled. For a moment the evening stayed quiet around us. "I wanted you once," she said. No performance. No trap.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "I know." "I thought wanting the greatest man in a room meant I understood him." I looked at her. She shook her head before I could answer. "Do not turn that into a boast. I am trying to be gracious." "Nigga, you chose difficult material." She laughed, and whatever remained awkward between us loosened into something we could both hold without bleeding on it.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: "I'm glad you're coming to the wedding," I said. "So am I." Shawna came down the steps carrying three glasses. She handed one to Vesper, one to me, and kept the third. "What are you two plotting?" "Curtains," Vesper said. "Cars," I said. My wife looked between us. "Terrible liars." She sat beside me anyway.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Across the garden, Bernard said something that made Magnolia laugh with her whole face. June showed Adrian a sketch and he kissed the top of her head. Tank came out of the kitchen carrying a cake sample Rosa had finally permitted him to eat. Everybody had keys now. To garages, houses, ships, stages, rooms they wanted to return to.

timeline.speaker: TICKET
timeline.text: Nigga, I had spent a lot of my life breaking doors. Watching my people choose which ones to open felt expensive in a way I intended to keep affording.
